Hey there! I've been working on this Automated Moderator program for awhile, and after weeks of testing in the subverses I moderate, /v/Voatocracy and /v/AutoModTestGrounds, I believe it is ready for a first release. Read below for how to use this and how it works!

What is This?

VoatAutoMod is a Java program that uses Selenium WebDriver to automatically use a browser to perform moderator functions. AutoMod was designed to help perform basic tasks for moderators to lighten the work load. VoatAutoMod MUST be run on a computer that has a GUI (no command-line only servers/computers), and it must have Firefox or Chrome installed (Firefox is recommended since it has better support for automation), and the computer must have the Java runtime environment installed. In order to edit and compile the files, JDK ~1.7 or ~1.8 must also be installed.

How Does This Work? I Thought Bots Don't Work on Voat?

Yes, it's nearly impossible for traditional bots to work on Voat, so AutoMod instead uses browser automation. In other words, AutoMod opens up a browser and controls it much like a user would, except much faster and all the time! There are also manual delays set up inside the AutoMod program so that AutoMod doesn't get tripped up by Voat's spam and DDoS protection.

What Can This Do?

With only modifying a few global variables, AutoMod is able to automatically tag posts, delete posts and comments if they contain a predefined bad word to look for, delete posts if the subverse is in link/text only mode, and leave a response stating why the post or comment was deleted. With a little more work, AutoMod can post submissions on predefined dates and times. With even more tweaking, AutoMod can send messages, post automatic responses when certain phrases are said, and other fun stuff!

How Do I Use This?

It is recommended to set up an alternate account for your AutoMod to use. You should also have a computer you can keep on 24/7 to run this, so either an old computer you have laying around, your desktop, or even a Raspberry Pi would work.

FOR PEOPLE USING A RASPBERRY PI:
I personally am running my version of AutoMod on my Raspberry Pi B, so here's my advice:
Install Pidora since Raspbian doesn't have Firefox. Older models of the RasPi only seem to work for about 48 hours before Firefox crashes due to memory limitations. Install Java and Firefox on your RasPi (click for instructions to install java). AutoMod should be set up on a separate computer (see below instructions), but instead of running, export the project as a runnable jar, then move the jar onto your RasPi and run using the terminal.

FOR PEOPLE WHO DON'T KNOW WHAT THEY'RE DOING:
1. Install the latest JDK for your system from here
2. Install Eclipse for your system from here
3. Download the .zip file from below and extract it
4. After reading through README.txt, move the VoatAutoMod_Release folder to your Eclipse workspace directory (this should be set up after starting Eclipse for the first time)
5. Start Eclipse and right click in the Project Explorer window, then select Import
6. In the Import window, select General>Existing Projects into Workspace, then click Next
7. Across from Select Root Directory, click Browse and navigate to where you saved the VoatAutoMod_Release folder
8. Click Finish to finish importing the project
9. In the Project Explorer, click the arrows to expand VoatAutoMod_Release>src>(default package)
10. Double click AutoMod.java to open it for editing
11. Scroll through and edit the values for subName, userName, and password for your subverse and account you want to use
12. Click the Run button at the top (looks like a green play button) to run the program
13. When you are finished, click the red square above the console to stop the program

FOR PEOPLE WHO KNOW WHAT THEY'RE DOING
Follow the above instructions, I'm confident you can figure it out if you're familiar with Java. Also check out the Javadocs for Selenium here to familiarize yourself with what Selenium can do and how it works.

Are There Limitations to This?

Yes! By default all users need to fill out reCaptchas to post submissions and send messages, but these restrictions are lifted once a user has enough CCP or posts enough content that people like (I don't know exactly how it works). If AutoMod encounters a reCaptcha, it'll crash! So if you're planning on having AutoMod post anything or send messages, make sure your account isn't restricted by reCaptchas first.

Help! AutoMod Crashed! What do I do!?

Before rerunning the program, please copy the console output and send it in a message to me! This will help me debug AutoMod and improve it for everyone. This is especially important as the new API is being rolled out. Once you've done that, you can close all instances of your browser and try running the program again. If it crashes immediately, please tell me and include the console output too!

I will try and provide technical support for this (and answer to Atko if this causes a huge influx of spambots), but try to keep in mind I'm just one guy. Have fun and happy Voating!

Since this is using browser automation, how does it find comments that match specified moderation policies? Does it keep re-checking threads until they're of a certain age?

By default it will recheck threads until they are either off the new page or older than 24 hours, I originally made it as a mod for smaller subs to use and moderate content for longer, while larger subs can use it as a filter that submissions pass through. It finds comments by searching for elements that match specifications as comments, then it reads through it to see if any of the bad words you set are in the comment. This checks without context so it will delete a comment if you set 'ho' as a bad word and the comment says 'how' or 'who'
